name: 🍅 Ratatouille
tagline: A big sheet pan of summer vegetables roasted sweet, then folded into a garlicky tomato sauce.

items.name: Italian seasoning or herbes de Provence
Sugar (only if the tomatoes taste sharp)

steps.text: Oven to 425°F. Line two sheet pans with foil.
Cut the eggplant, zucchini, squash and peppers into 3/4-inch cubes, about the same size so they cook evenly.
Toss the vegetables with most of the olive oil, the seasoning, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Spread in one layer across both pans.
Roast until browned at the edges, stirring once halfway.
Meanwhile, cook the chopped onion in the rest of the oil in a big pot over medium until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer while the vegetables roast. Taste: a pinch of sugar if it's sharp.
Fold the roasted vegetables into the sauce and simmer together for 5 minutes.
Top with parmesan and serve with warm crusty bread.

kid_jobs.job: Wash the vegetables and cut the soft ones (zucchini, squash) with a kid knife
Toss the vegetables with oil and seasoning in a big bowl
Sprinkle the parmesan and set the table

chef_tip: Roast, don't stew. Two pans with room between the pieces give browned, sweet vegetables instead of a soggy pot.
make_ahead: Better the next day. Make it up to 2 days ahead and warm it gently on the stove.
leftovers: Lunch over pasta or rice, or warm it in a skillet, make wells and crack in eggs for a quick shakshuka.
swaps: Fresh tomatoes: 5–6 ripe ones, chopped, instead of the can
Add Italian sausage or chicken for more protein
Serve over polenta, pasta or rice instead of bread
serve_with: Crusty bread, or over pasta, polenta or rice
heads_up: Oven to 425°F before you start chopping.

game_plan.what: Oven to 425°F. Kids wash the vegetables.
Cut and toss the vegetables; into the oven.
Onion and garlic in the pot, then the tomatoes. Stir the pans.
Vegetables into the sauce. Kids warm the bread.
Kids set out parmesan and the bread.
